title: Animating a Backflip: from blocking to animation
summary: The blockout turned into animation, as the tutor does it in the graph editor: all keys Bezier with auto clamped handles (the IK/FK switch stays constant), the end sped up, the body's backward travel linear in the air (you can't slow down in the air) and its height and spin leaving the take-off and hitting the landing with vector handles, the wind-up eased at 36/36 like Graph Pilot, the legs' tuck released sharply before the landing, the feet pointing as he takes off and reaching for the floor (vector: they snap back), the arms carrying the spin into the landing, the elbows a few frames behind the upper arms (overlapping action), and the timing fixed: the slow beginning scaled in from frame 1 and the rest moved in after it.
expected_result: The same backflip, now smooth: a quick wind-up, a fast spin with the knees tucked, the legs snapping out to land half a metre behind, the arms swinging through; about 1.9 s at 60 fps.

steps.note: the blockout done: select all bones (A), all keys (A), T > Bezier, V > Auto Clamped
except the IK/FK switch: it stays a switch (constant), or the legs would drift between IK and FK for thirty frames
the end is too slow: the keys after the landing pulled in (S X from the landing frame)
the main control first -- in the air you can't slow down: the backward motion is linear from take-off to landing
the height and the spin leave the take-off and hit the landing at full speed: vector handles (you don't slow down before you land)
the height and the spin leave the take-off and hit the landing at full speed: vector handles (you don't slow down before you land)
the wind-up eased in and out (Graph Pilot, both at 36)
legs: tucked in, then the tuck released -- boom, the floor: vector, no slowing down
the feet: extended as he takes off, back to normal, pointing for the floor, straight as he lands
they stayed extended too long: vector handles, they correct as fast as possible
arms: as he lands the outgoing handles are vector, all the speed of the rotation
overlapping action: the elbows keep going after the upper arms stop -- their keys a few frames later
the beginning is way too slow: a marker at the take-off, everything before it scaled in from frame 1 (2D cursor pivot, S X)
then everything after it moved in (G X)
the frame range to the new end
